correctness.rationale: For a commuting-permutation braid solution, the automorphism group is exactly C_Sym(X)(f,g) and contains the elementary-abelian group H generated by f,g. The H-set orbit-type centralizer decomposition is a direct product of wreath products. Requiring every factor to be elementary abelian forces at most one orbit of each proper subgroup type and, only in p=2, a pair of fixed points; the rank is a+2b+e and yields all finite-rank limits. The universal faithful-action bound |X|>=pr and forced free orbit for odd p,r>p+1 give the sharp cardinalities. Explicit commuting shifts produce equality in every case. Boundary cases p=2,r=1 and r=6, odd p,r=p+1,p+2,p+3 checked; finite checker passes but proof does not rely on finite tests.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating literature explicitly asks about smallest automorphism-realization sizes. This theorem determines the complete exact minimum-size function in a natural nondegenerate permutation subclass, shows that this subclass cannot realize elementary-abelian ranks beyond a sharp prime-dependent cutoff even on arbitrarily large sets, and isolates an exceptional binary fixed-pair phenomenon. Its projective-line orbit optimization and infinite no-go result are not a renaming of one small computation.
